messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'hotpool-eu-1' > 95% util and queue depth spiking. 429 rate on user-facing endpoints increasing. Auto-scaler failing to add capacity (max_pools reached). Investigate. thread:1749995555

oncall-rotation: I'm taking this. paging @sanjay @emily @kyle for triage. brief pls on current impact.

sanjay: on it, joining. seeing a steady queue growth across hotpool-eu-1 and hotpool-us-west-2. autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but the pool allocation RPCs are returning 409 / quota-exhausted.

emily: can we confirm which rate policies are kicking in? I see a ton of 429s from edge logs with reason=RATE_LIMIT_TIERS.

sanjay: right — token bucket metrics show token refill stalled for tier=standard-hot. refill_rate dropped to 0.0 during the spike. suspect misapplied ratewindow config from yesterday's rollout.

kyle: @sanjay paste the binder of the token config pls. if it's a >0 refill_rate we need to check allocator.

sanjay: pasting snippet from the live config:```json
{"tier":"standard-hot","burst_capacity":50,"refill_rate":0.0,"window_secs":60}
```

sanjay: that refill_rate should be 10.0. looks like a bad merge in infra-configs-deploy.

lia: from support side, we've got ~7 customers reporting elevated tail latency and 3 customers seeing 429 spikes. one large customer (acme-corp) reported timeouts in their payments flow. escalation ops notified.

customer-support: Acme reported 15 failed requests in last 10m, severity P1 for them. They ask for ETA and mitigation steps.

oncall-rotation: ok immediate plan: 1) revert the recent ratewindow config change for standard-hot (hotfix). 2) temporarily increase pool quota for hotpool-eu-1 to allow autoscaler to bind. 3) enable fallback routing to secondary pool hotpool-eu-1-fallback for non-sensitive traffic. 4) inform customers. who can run the hotfix?

emily: I can push the hotfix to infra-configs-rolling. will revert the token refill_rate to 10.0 and roll to both regions. pushing now.

ops-bot: deploy started by emily - infra-configs-rolling @ 1749995698. CI: passed, applying to cluster 'eu-1' then 'us-west-2'.

sanjay: while we wait, can we temporarily lower the tokenbucket min-reserve to allow bursts? current min_reserve=20. lowering to 5 will reduce immediate 429s but increases risk of overload.

kyle: agree acceptable as short term. I'll patch policy to min_reserve=5 for 10 minutes. command: ```curl -XPOST https://control.redwood.internal/policies/standard-hot/patch -d '{"min_reserve":5,"ttl":600}'```

ops-bot: policy patch applied by kyle @ 1749995745.

emily: hotfix rolled to eu-1 at 1749995752. refill_rate restored to 10.0. monitoring token refill — metrics showing tokens ramping back up.

sanjay: autoscaler still failing to allocate new nodes due to pool quota. submitting quota bump to platform control plane now.

ops-bot: quota bump request accepted (req-88923) and applied to hotpool-eu-1 @ 1749995790.

lia: customers: Acme notified via PM with mitigation steps and ETA ~10m. support thread updated.

oncall-rotation: seeing 429 rate drop and queue draining. tail latencies returning to baseline for most customers. can we confirm ACME's errors cleared?

customer-support: ACME confirms flows passing now. they saw intermittent errors between 10:12-10:18 UTC. marked as resolved from their end.

emily: follow-ups: revert the temporary min_reserve change after 10m (kyle), create a postmortem entry, and add a guard in infra-configs CI to prevent refill_rate=0.0 for any hot tier.

sanjay: logging note: need better detection rule for token refill stalls — alert when refill_rate < 1.0 for >60s.

kyle: will revert min_reserve at 1749996350 (in 10m) and postops will verify no regression.

oncall-rotation: taking owner for postmortem. will schedule follow-up with config, autoscale, and policy owners. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: hotpool-eu-1 saturation mitigated, root cause preliminary: bad merge set refill_rate=0.0 for standard-hot tier; secondary contributor: pool quota hit prevented autoscaler from adding capacity. Next steps: postmortem, CI guard, alert tuning.
